youtube.title: 🔥 Meta Just Open Sourced Their Internal Design System
youtube.description: Astryx is Meta's battle-tested design system that powered 13,000+ internal apps for eight years — and now it's open source. Unlike every other design system that locks you into wrapper components and custom build configs, Astryx lets you theme with CSS custom properties and override with whatever styling you already use: Tailwind, CSS modules, or plain CSS. You get 150 accessible components, seven ready-made themes, dark mode, templates, and a CLI that scaffolds complete patterns like data tables and form wizards in seconds. No build plugin required — just import the CSS and start using typed React components. The architecture is designed for both human developers and AI assistants to work from the same docs and conventions, making onboarding instant whether you're a person or an agent. Search 'facebook astryx' on GitHub to see how Meta solved design system customization without the usual styling wars.

linkedin.text:
Every design system locks you into their styling opinions.

You wrap components. Override props that fight you. Maintain a fork just to match your brand colors. Your designer wants one shade lighter and you're back in the wrapper hell.

🚨 Meta just open sourced the design system that powered 13,000+ internal apps for 8 years — and it works completely differently.

Astryx solves customization without the usual wrapper nightmare:

✅ Theme with CSS custom properties, not component wrappers
✅ Override with Tailwind, CSS modules, or plain CSS you already use  
✅ 150 accessible components, 7 ready themes, dark mode, CLI scaffolding

No build plugin. No PostCSS config. Just import the CSS and use typed React components.

The architecture is designed so people and AI assistants build from the same docs and conventions. When your designer changes the brand, they edit CSS variables — your React stays untouched.

⭐ 13,000 teams at Meta shipped faster because Astryx made customization effortless instead of a fight.

Search 'facebook astryx' on GitHub to see Meta's solution to design system lock-in.

Have you ever forked a design system just to change the colors?
